name_full: d-APV (stored in the catalogue as D-Ap5)
label: Full competitive NMDA-receptor block, the reference control
action: Competitive block of the glutamate site: the control against which any negative modulator is read.
rationale: It abolishes the spontaneous bursts, so it fixes how much NMDA-receptor current must go before the burst stops.
open_premise: That the burst needs NMDA-receptor activity does not show a gain of receptor function.
counter: Against the wild-type floor about 20 percent of the delayed evoked response remains under it, which is not evidence of incomplete block.
next_test: Measure the abolition threshold (percent of isolated NMDA-receptor current removed) with measured bath magnesium; this is the first number every NAM comparison needs.

label: Ifenprodil-site GluN2B negative modulator, used as a tool
action: Negative allosteric modulation of GluN2B-containing receptors at the ifenprodil site.
rationale: A burst effect at a smaller removed fraction than the control needs would make a GluN2B-directed comparison the better question.
open_premise: The removable share of such a modulator is bounded by receptor composition and zinc, so a plateau below the control is unresolved, not support for total gain.
counter: The compound's GluN2B rows are measured activities, not a curated mechanism, and other targets are also measured; selectivity is not assessed.
next_test: Measure its removable fraction in the isolated NMDA-receptor current first; compare with the control only up to that fraction. A second modulator of the same site controls chemotype only.

label: AMPA/kainate block arm, tools not yet qualified
action: Block of AMPA and kainate receptors to test whether the burst survives.
rationale: Survival of the burst under a verified block would remove an AMPA contribution; abolition alone cannot separate AMPA drive from loss of magnesium relief.
open_premise: Whether an AMPA-dependent component exists at all.
counter: Two GYKI compounds are registered under one label (different structures); the mechanism papers of two tools are unread; kainate is not separated.
next_test: Qualify tool identity and selectivity first (science package in progress), then test survival under a block verified by the fast current.

label: Ih (HCN) blocker as a tool arm, after matched-condition recordings
action: Block of the hyperpolarisation-activated current, two chemotypes, engagement shown first.
rationale: Only worth running if sag and rebound stay larger at matched potential and deflection.
open_premise: Whether any HCN contribution remains after matching; no benefit is claimed.
counter: A blocker response shows contribution as in normal cortex, not a defect; the passive-size reading is the rival; the sodium action of one tool is an off-target.
next_test: Run the matched-condition recording with capacitance and access resistance first; no HCN compound is nominated before it.

label: Clinical-stage GluN2B negative modulator with species-dependent maximum
action: Negative modulation of GluN2B-containing receptors; maximum inhibition 82 percent on rat GluN1/GluN2B against 45 percent on rat triheteromers (human GluN1/GluN2B 91 percent).
rationale: A compound with human exposure that could serve as the in-slice modulator once the tool result is in.
open_premise: That the ceiling seen in oocytes holds in the slice; its washout is very slow in oocytes.
counter: The selectivity statement rests on a supplementary figure that was not read; slice precedent is a different region and age.
next_test: Use only after V02 shows a removable fraction; read the fraction at the burst, not in oocytes.

label: Human-exposure GluN2B negative modulator found by the search, site not recorded
action: Negative modulation of the GluN2B subunit (registry pIC50 about 8.1-8.3, selectivity not determined).
rationale: A second modulator with human exposure could extend the comparison, if it acts at the ifenprodil site.
open_premise: Whether it shares the ifenprodil site and the triheteromer ceiling; the registry gives no receptor site.
counter: Abstract-level source only: a phase 2 study in adults with depression; no assay text in the registry row.
next_test: Find a primary source stating its site and maximum effect on triheteromers (public, in silico); until then it is not a same-site control.

label: pH-dependent GluN2B modulator: a condition to state, not a candidate
action: Inhibition of GluN2B-containing receptors, stronger at acidic pH (registry value measured at pH 6.9).
rationale: It shows that GluN2B-directed potency can depend on the bath pH.
open_premise: Whether ifenprodil-site modulators in general depend on pH enough to matter in the slice.
counter: Phase 1 in healthy volunteers only (abstract); registry selectivity not determined.
next_test: State and match the bath pH in every arm; check the literature on pH dependence of the tool actually used.

label: Class recorded on a GluN1/GluN2B assembly record, no maximum effect
action: Antagonism recorded on the two-gene GRIN1/GRIN2B record of a curated mechanism table.
rationale: Possible chemotype controls if V02 and V05 do not give one.
open_premise: That an assembly record means subunit selectivity: it names where the mechanism was attached, not how selective the molecule is.
counter: No maximum effect, species or assay context in the catalogue; none approved.
next_test: Read primary sources for maximum effect and site only if a further chemotype is needed.

label: Registry row under GluN2B whose assay was on GluN2C
action: Recorded as a negative modulator under a rat GluN2B entry.
open_premise: The assay text says the receptor was co-expressed with GluN2C; the value is not a GluN2B measurement.
counter: Filing under a target does not make the measurement the target's; no transfer is made.
next_test: None; kept so the filing is not mistaken for evidence.

label: Kv7 opening and gap-junction block: abstain
action: Opening of Kv7 channels, or block of connexin and pannexin channels, proposed in earlier readings.
rationale: A response would not show a defect of the target in these cells.
open_premise: That a leak deficit or coupling drives the burst: neither is shown; the burst fall under the gap-junction tool has no supporting datum for coupling.
counter: Smaller cells with a seal leak and effects on synaptic currents explain the same observations.
next_test: Nominate nothing before a difference current reversing near the potassium equilibrium potential and a matched-effect control that fails to reproduce the fall.
